headline: Off-Highway deal drives sales up, but profit slips
summary_short: Q2 net sales rose 92% year over year to $1,566 million on the newly acquired Allison Off-Highway business, while net income fell 7% to $181 million and diluted EPS dropped 6% to $2.15 on acquisition-related costs and higher interest expense.
summary_long: Net sales growth was almost entirely inorganic: Allison Off-Highway (acquired January 1, 2026 from Dana) contributed $706 million, while legacy Allison Transmission grew 6% to a record $860 million on Defense and North American truck demand. Gross margin held near 33%. Net income fell 7% y/y on higher SG&A, D&A, and interest expense from acquisition financing, plus mark-to-market losses on securities; adjusted diluted EPS still grew 8% to $2.73. Cash fell to $399 million and long-term debt rose to $4,094 million on acquisition financing, though Allison repaid $150 million on its revolver and repurchased $46 million of stock. Full-year 2026 guidance was raised across sales, EBITDA, net income, cash flow, and free cash flow.

drivers.explanation: Results were reshaped by the Allison Off-Highway acquisition, which drove the sales and EBITDA growth but also added D&A, interest expense, and integration costs that pulled GAAP net income down y/y.

Net sales rose on the addition of the Allison Off-Highway business ($706M), while legacy Allison Transmission grew 6% to a record $860M on Defense end-market growth and North American truck market momentum.
Gross profit growth was principally driven by the addition of the Allison Off-Highway business unit.
Consolidated cost of sales rose almost entirely from including the newly acquired Off-Highway segment's $588M cost of sales this quarter, which has no year-ago comparable.

Decrease was driven by higher operating costs (including increased D&A) from the Off-Highway acquisition, plus higher net interest expense and unrealized mark-to-market losses on marketable securities.
Cash fell mainly on the $2,529M net cash outlay for the Off-Highway acquisition, partly offset by new debt and financing inflows raised to fund it.
Debt rose y/y to fund the Off-Highway acquisition; within the quarter the company reduced debt by repaying the remaining $150M outstanding on its revolving credit facility.
